title: Matrix-shape-aware attention kernel calibration and staged decode stabilization
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Problem statement: When integrating FlashAttention v3 fallbacks alongside v2, we observed intermittent 95th/99th latency regressions on medium-length (512–2048) sequences during startup and bursty traffic. Root causes are a combination of suboptimal kernel choice for specific (B, S, H) matrix shapes, mismatched workspace allocation heuristics, and abrupt kernel handoffs mid-decode. This ticket aims to implement a matrix-shape-aware calibration pass at model load time and a staged decode stabilization policy that enforces a short-term hysteresis window for kernel switching to avoid oscillation and tail latency spikes.
technical_notes: 1) Calibration: Add a lightweight calibration routine executed once per model-version instance that samples the common batch size and sequence length pairs from observed telemetry and runs microbenchmarks to estimate cost models for candidate kernels (v2, v3, fallback). Store calibration table keyed by (batch_range, seq_range, head_dim) with preferred kernel and expected cold/warm latency. 2) Kernel Preference Scoring: Implement a shape-aware scorer that combines calibrated latency, workspace footprint, and degradation probability. Score function must be deterministic and cheaply computable at request-time. 3) Staged Decode Stabilization: Introduce 'kernel stickiness' during the first N decode tokens for a new request (configurable by model) and a short cross-request cooldown period to prevent rapid kernel oscillation under bursty traffic. 4) Workspace Strategy: When calibration predicts marginal gains but workspace reallocation cost is high, prefer a lower-latency kernel that reuses current allocator to avoid allocation thrash. 5) Telemetry: Emit events for calibration decisions, kernel switches, and stabilization-triggered fallbacks. Include counters for oscillation events and tail latency deltas.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Calibration routine runs during model load with <200ms median overhead for common models. 2) In canary traffic (10% of capacity) 99th latency for sequences 512–2048 decreases by at least 15% vs baseline with previous runtime. 3) Kernel switch oscillation events reduce to <1 per 10k requests in burst scenarios. 4) No regression in throughput on steady-state workloads (within 3% of baseline). 5) Telemetry events contain shape keys and decision reasons and are queryable in Console within 2 hours.
tests_and_benchmarks: - Synthetic harness: run matrix sweep of (B in 1,2,4,8), (S in 128,256,512,1024,2048), (H in 64,128) comparing v2/v3/fallback kernels. - Canary: route 10% of real traffic for three days and collect p50/p95/p99, allocation churn, and kernel switch counts. - Stress: burst traffic with inter-arrival times at 5x baseline to reproduce oscillation. - Regression: run existing perf suite for runtime-1.22 and compare token/sec. - PR contains deterministic microbenchmarks and CI job to validate calibration table format and scorer determinism.
notes_on_tradeoffs: We prioritize tail latency stability over absolute best-case throughput for short startup windows. That means in some shape bins we will intentionally select a slightly slower kernel if it avoids workspace churn or reduces switch probability. This increases code complexity (calibration tables, scorer) but yields predictable SLOs. Long-term we can explore ML-based scorer but will ship deterministic heuristics first.
comments: 2025-02-12: Initial spike identified in telemetry dashboard: p99 jump correlated with deployments that enable v3 on a subset of machines. Logged incident and created this ticket. - Aisha

2025-02-18: Spike reproduced locally with synthetic harness. Observed kernel handoffs mid-decode when sequence length prediction heuristics disagree. Attached trace: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4212

2025-02-22: Implemented prototype calibration pass (branch: feat/shape-calib). Microbenchmarks added; calibration format is CSV-like keyed by seq_range. Pushed early numbers to perf board: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Shape+Calibration+Draft

2025-02-26: Design review with runtime and infra teams. Decided on scorer inputs: {calibrated_latency_ms, workspace_bytes_delta, historical_switch_rate}. Action: Liam to implement scorer and staged-stability middleware. - Design notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-shape-calib-design

2025-03-01: Canary rollout started (10% traffic) with staged-stability enabled. Early results: p99 down 12% for 512–1024 sequences but 1.8% throughput drop on large-batch workloads; investigating allocator reuse path. - Liam

2025-03-04: Fixed allocator reuse path to avoid extra memcpy on workspace resize. Re-ran canary: p99 now down 18% for target shapes, throughput impact reduced to 0.6%. Preparing PR for runtime-1.22. Linking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4299
2025-03-05: Ready for review. Checklist: unit tests, deterministic scorer property tests, telemetry schema migration ticket opened (ENG-873211). - Liam
